hero.filename: USS Mount Hood (AE-11) explodes at Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
hero.caption: The explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands on 10 November 1944. The smoke trails are left by fragments ejected by the explosion. The cause of the explosion could not be determined.
hero.alt: The explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands on 10 November 1944. The smoke trails are left by fragments ejected by the explosion. The cause of the explosion could not be determined.
hero.artist: U.S. Navy, photographed by a photographer of the 57th Construction Battalion, who had set up his camera to take pictures of the Battalion's camp.
categories: Seeadler Harbor in World War II

images.filename: Aerial view of USS Mindanao (ARG-3) after the explosion of USS Mount Hood (AE-11) at Seeadler Harbor on 10 November 1944.jpg
images.caption: Explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944: Small craft gathered around the internal combustion engine repair ship USS Mindanao (ARG-3) during salvage and rescue efforts shortly after Mount Hood blew up about 350 yards away from Mindanao's port side. Mindanao, and seven motor minesweepers (YMS) moored to her starboard side, were damaged by the blast, as were the attack transport USS Alhena (AKA-9), in the photo's top left center, and the destroyer escort USS Oberrender (DE-344), in top right. Note the extensive oil slick, with tracks through it made by small craft.
images.alt: Explosion of the U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944: Small craft gathered around the internal combustion engine repair ship USS Mindanao (ARG-3) during salvage and rescue efforts shortly after Mount Hood blew up about 350 yards away from Mindanao's port side. Mindanao, and seven motor minesweepers (YMS) moored to her starboard side, were damaged by the blast, as were the attack transport USS Alhena (AKA-9), in the photo's top left center, and the destroyer escort USS Oberrender (DE-344), in top right. Note the extensive oil slick, with tracks through it made by small craft.

images.filename: USS Mount Hood (AE-11) explodes in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944 (NH 95404).jpg
images.caption: The U.S. Navy ammunition ship USS Mount Hood (AE-11) explodes in Seeadler Harbor, Manus, Admiralty Islands, 10 November 1944, as seen from the Naval Supply Depot on Manus. The internal combustion engine repair ship USS Mindanao (ARG-3) is visible at the base of the cloud, the attack transport USS Alhena (AKA-9) is to her right.
